C-LANGUAGE-SCAFFOLDING.Summary: Deploy the approved language scaffolding: mirrored en and ru source roots with canonical English records, truthful translation fallback, and the existing bilingual static portal.
C-LANGUAGE-SCAFFOLDING.Problem: Source Markdown is monolingual and language-independent even though the portal already has en and ru routes. Moving files alone would break source links and would not select reviewed translations.

Goals.Goal: Move the existing charter, Registry, Portfolio, and explanatory Markdown into en roots and prepare matching ru folders.
Make the renderer select a reviewed language source, keep counterpart routes and stable clause anchors, and expose missing translations honestly.
Commit and push the verified source and generated output, publish through the existing deployment tool, and verify the served manifest.

Constraints.Constraint: English source edition 2.2 and individual document revisions remain authoritative; preserve policy meaning and record facts.
One record identity and approval history across languages; Russian content records its English source revision and hash.
Keep shared UI messages and authored bilingual chrome; keep assets shared and the existing English default.
Preserve unrelated dirty workspace changes; publish from an isolated clean checkout if needed.

The current user instruction "lets deploy this scaffolding" approves the preceding proposed layout and authorizes this implementation, lifecycle completion, commits, pushes, and deployment after verification.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Translate the corpus or invent Russian policy wording.
Publish live Registry records or change decisions, approvals, policy, hosting, or access controls.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: All English source files have one canonical en location; ru folders contain scaffolding without English duplicates presented as translations.

Reviewed translations render on their language route with the correct text language, metadata, diagrams, search content, and counterpart links. Missing or draft translations fall back visibly to English; stale reviewed translations fail validation.
Source links, page routing, source manifest, and maintenance documentation resolve after relocation.
The real build and deterministic site checks pass; focused tests prove language selection and error behavior.
The deployed manifest matches the committed generated output, and unrelated workspace changes remain untouched.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Language-source fixtures, preserved English content, resolved generated links and anchors, repeatable output, and the deployment tool served-manifest verification.
